issue.standard_remedy: Harmonize prices to the best plant / global agreement
issue.summary: Pays 13% on average above the best plant for the same materials

plan.diagnosis: Stuttgart plant pays 13% average premium above best-plant pricing across 238 materials sourced from Meridian Industrial GmbH in SAP S/4HANA, resulting in USD 4,142,282 excess spend over the trailing 12 months. Root cause is lack of price harmonization and probable absence of a global or multi-plant agreement that would extend best-negotiated rates to all locations.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct price benchmark analysis across all plants purchasing the 238 materials from Meridian Industrial GmbH to identify best-plant pricing and document the 13% gap
Initiate commercial negotiation with Meridian Industrial GmbH to establish global or multi-plant agreement extending best-plant pricing to Stuttgart and all other facilities

Update SAP S/4HANA info records (EINE table) for all 238 materials at Stuttgart plant to reflect harmonized pricing; create or update outline agreements (contracts/scheduling agreements) with new rates
Implement price variance monitoring dashboard in SAP S/4HANA to track Stuttgart vs. best-plant pricing monthly and trigger alerts if deviation exceeds 3%
Establish governance process requiring all new Meridian Industrial GmbH purchases to reference global agreement and blocking local info record creation without Category Manager approval

plan.expected_impact: Price harmonization to best-plant rates will eliminate the 13% premium and deliver USD 4,142,282 in annual savings.
kpis: Stuttgart plant price premium vs. best plant (target: 0% within 90 days)
Realized savings from harmonized pricing (target: USD 4,142,282 annualized)
Percentage of 238 materials updated to harmonized rates (target: 100% by Week 8)
Price variance incidents flagged by monitoring dashboard (target: <5 per quarter post-implementation)
risks: Meridian Industrial GmbH may resist global pricing, requiring escalation or competitive sourcing action
Stuttgart plant may have unique material specifications or service requirements justifying premium pricing for subset of materials
Implementation delays in SAP master data updates could defer savings realization beyond Q1 2027
Demand volatility at Stuttgart may impact negotiating leverage if volumes decline
erp_actions: SAP S/4HANA: Update purchasing info records (table EINE) for 238 materials at Stuttgart plant (WERKS) to harmonized pricing effective date
SAP S/4HANA: Create or amend outline agreement (ME31K/ME32K) referencing global contract with Meridian Industrial GmbH covering all plants
SAP S/4HANA: Establish source list entries (ME01) for the 238 materials at Stuttgart plant pointing to the global agreement, set MRP-relevant flag
SAP S/4HANA: Configure price variance tolerance (OME4) to 3% for Stuttgart plant and activate exception alerts in procurement cockpit
SAP S/4HANA: Apply info record creation authorization restrictions (authorization object M_EINF_WRK) to prevent Stuttgart buyers from creating local pricing without approval workflow
